notice.line.label.description: How a notice names the line or lines it is about, by TfL's mode. `lines` is their names, joined with commas ("Northern", "333, 415"), and `count` how many. A Tube line's name comes without "line".
notice.line.label.en: {mode, select, bus {{count, plural, one {Bus {lines}} other {Buses {lines}}}} tube {{lines} line} other {{lines}}}
notice.line.label.nb: {mode, select, bus {{count, plural, one {Buss {lines}} other {Buss {lines}}}} tube {{lines}-linjen} other {{lines}}}

notice.line.status.description: What is wrong on a line, in a word or two, for a notice's title. `status` is the key for TfL's status: suspended (Suspended), part_suspended (Part Suspended), severe_delays (Severe Delays), issues (Issues Reported), closed (Closed, Planned Closure), part_closed (Part Closure), not_running (Not Running).
notice.line.status.en: {status, select, suspended {Suspended} part_suspended {Part suspended} severe_delays {Severe delays} issues {Issues} closed {Closed} part_closed {Part closed} not_running {Not running} other {Disrupted}}
notice.line.status.nb: {status, select, suspended {Innstilt} part_suspended {Delvis innstilt} severe_delays {Store forsinkelser} issues {Problemer} closed {Stengt} part_closed {Delvis stengt} not_running {Kjører ikke} other {Avvik}}

notice.line.title.description: The title of a line's notice: `label` is notice.line.label's, `status` notice.line.status's ("Northern line: Severe delays"). Its summary is the provider's own text, shortened.

notice.line.tag.description: The tag in front of a line's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen): a bus route's (`mode` bus, `count` 1, `line` its number), several routes with one notice (`mode` bus, `count` more), or any other line's own name.
notice.line.tag.en: {mode, select, bus {{count, plural, one {Bus {line}} other {Buses}}} other {{line}}}
notice.line.tag.nb: {mode, select, bus {{count, plural, one {{line}-bussen} other {Busser}}} other {{line}}}

notice.station.title.description: The title of the notice for something wrong at a TfL stop (a lift out of order, an entrance closed): `station` is the stop's name without "Underground Station", "Rail Station" or "DLR Station" at its end ("Elephant & Castle"). Its summary is TfL's description of it, without the station's name in capitals TfL leads it with, shortened.

notice.station.text.description: Something wrong at a TfL stop in one line, where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen, after the tag TfL): `station` as notice.station.title's, `detail` TfL's description without the station's name it leads with ("Elephant & Castle: No step-free access to the Northern line").

notice.road.title.description: The title of the notice for a serious or severe road disruption TfL reports near the postcode. Its summary is notice.road.text's, shortened.

notice.road.tag.description: The tag in front of a road disruption's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen).

notice.road.text.description: A road disruption in one line: `category` is TfL's for it ("Works", "Collisions"), `comments` TfL's comments on it, each as TfL wrote it.

notice.flood.title.description: What one of the Environment Agency's flood warnings is, by its level: `level` is severe (its severityLevel 1, a severe flood warning), warning (2, a flood warning) or alert (3, a flood alert). A warning no longer in force (4) has no notice. The title of its notice, whose summary is the flood area the EA names it for ("River Thames at Southwark").
notice.flood.title.en: {level, select, severe {Severe flood warning} warning {Flood warning} alert {Flood alert} other {Flood warning}}
notice.flood.title.nb: {level, select, severe {Alvorlig flomfare} warning {Flomfare} alert {Flomvarsel} other {Flomfare}}

notice.flood.tag.description: The tag in front of a flood warning's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen).

notice.flood.text.description: A flood warning in one line, after notice.flood.tag: `title` is notice.flood.title's, `area` the flood area the EA names it for ("Flood warning: River Thames at Southwark").

notice.weather.title.description: The title of a weather warning's notice, the Met Office's or MET Norway's. Its summary is notice.weather.warning's, and when it applies (notice.until).

notice.weather.warning.description: A weather warning in a few words: `colour` is its level (red, amber or yellow, the Met Office's; red, orange or yellow, MET Norway's) and `hazard` what it warns of, in lower case ("wind", "rain"), as the warning names it (the Met Office's title, MetAlerts' eventAwarenessName or event).
notice.weather.warning.en: {colour, select, red {Red warning: {hazard}} amber {Amber warning: {hazard}} orange {Orange warning: {hazard}} yellow {Yellow warning: {hazard}} other {Warning: {hazard}}}
notice.weather.warning.nb: {colour, select, red {Rødt farevarsel: {hazard}} amber {Oransje farevarsel: {hazard}} orange {Oransje farevarsel: {hazard}} yellow {Gult farevarsel: {hazard}} other {Farevarsel: {hazard}}}

notice.until.description: Until when something applies, after what it is ("Amber warning: wind until Fri 21:00"). `when` is a time, a day, or a day and a time, already formatted; for MET Norway's warnings, the day it ends on, in Norway's time ("Fri"), the board adding the time in the screen's clock format.

notice.holiday.title.description: The title of the notice for the next bank holiday. Its summary is notice.holiday.summary's.

notice.holiday.tag.description: The tag in front of a bank holiday's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen).

notice.holiday.summary.description: The next bank holiday under its title: `when` is notice.day.today's, notice.day.tomorrow's or its date, `name` the holiday's own ("Fri 25 Dec – Christmas Day").

notice.holiday.text.description: The next bank holiday in one line, after notice.holiday.tag: `when` and `name` as notice.holiday.summary's ("Tomorrow: Christmas Day").

notice.holiday.text_with_notes.description: notice.holiday.text for a holiday GOV.UK has a note on: `notes` is the note, in lower case ("Today: Boxing Day (substitute day)").

notice.clock.title.description: The title of the reminder, in the week before, that the clocks go forward or back in the screen's time zone. Its summary is notice.clock.text's.

notice.clock.tag.description: The tag in front of the clock change's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen).

notice.clock.text.description: When the clocks change: `direction` is forward (an hour on, in the spring) or back (in the autumn), and `when` notice.clock.tonight's or notice.clock.on's. It ends before the time, which the screen adds after it in its own clock format, as it is just before the change ("Clocks go back an hour tonight, at 02:00").
notice.clock.text.en: {direction, select, forward {Clocks go forward an hour {when}, at} back {Clocks go back an hour {when}, at} other {Clocks change an hour {when}, at}}
notice.clock.text.nb: {direction, select, forward {Klokken stilles frem en time {when}, kl.} back {Klokken stilles tilbake en time {when}, kl.} other {Klokken stilles en time {when}, kl.}}

notice.clock.tonight.description: When the clocks change, in notice.clock.text, when it's in the coming night: the change is on today's or tomorrow's date, in the small hours.

notice.clock.on.description: When the clocks change, in notice.clock.text, on a later day: `day` is its date, already formatted ("Sun 25 Oct", in Norwegian "søn. 25. okt.").

notice.holiday.public_title.description: The title of the notice for Norway's next public holiday (a helligdag or 1 May, 17 May), for a Norwegian postcode, where notice.holiday.title is the UK's bank holidays'. Its summary is notice.holiday.summary's, with notice.holiday.name's.

notice.holiday.public_tag.description: The tag in front of a Norwegian public holiday's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen), as notice.holiday.tag is a UK bank holiday's. Its text is notice.holiday.text's, with notice.holiday.name's.

notice.holiday.name.description: A Norwegian public holiday's name, by its key: new_year (1 January), maundy_thursday, good_friday, easter_sunday, easter_monday, labour_day (1 May), constitution_day (17 May), ascension_day, whit_sunday, whit_monday, christmas_day (25 December) and boxing_day (26 December). The device works out when each falls (from Easter) itself; gov.uk names the UK's.
notice.holiday.name.en: {holiday, select, new_year {New Year’s Day} maundy_thursday {Maundy Thursday} good_friday {Good Friday} easter_sunday {Easter Sunday} easter_monday {Easter Monday} labour_day {Labour Day} constitution_day {Constitution Day} ascension_day {Ascension Day} whit_sunday {Whit Sunday} whit_monday {Whit Monday} christmas_day {Christmas Day} boxing_day {Boxing Day} other {Public holiday}}
notice.holiday.name.nb: {holiday, select, new_year {Første nyttårsdag} maundy_thursday {Skjærtorsdag} good_friday {Langfredag} easter_sunday {1. påskedag} easter_monday {2. påskedag} labour_day {Arbeidernes dag} constitution_day {Grunnlovsdag} ascension_day {Kristi himmelfartsdag} whit_sunday {Første pinsedag} whit_monday {Andre pinsedag} christmas_day {1. juledag} boxing_day {2. juledag} other {Helligdag}}

notice.day.today.description: The day something is on, when it's today; starts a line.

notice.day.tomorrow.description: The day something is on, when it's tomorrow; starts a line.

notice.bins.title.description: The title of the notice for a household's next bin collection, for a Norwegian board with an address set. Its summary is notice.bins.summary's.

notice.bins.tag.description: The tag in front of the next bin collection's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen). Its text is notice.bins.text's.

notice.bins.summary.description: The next bin collection under its title: `when` is notice.day.today's, notice.day.tomorrow's or its date, `fractions` the kinds of waste emptied that day, each notice.bins.fraction's, joined with commas ("Thu 26 Nov – Paper, Residual waste").

notice.bins.text.description: The next bin collection in one line, after notice.bins.tag: `when` and `fractions` as notice.bins.summary's ("Tomorrow: Paper, Residual waste").

notice.bins.fraction.description: A kind of waste, by Binable's key for it (BinCollection's fraction): paper, bio (food waste), residualWaste (and its less frequent and container collections), reusableMaterials (plastic and other packaging), glassContainer (glass and metal), christmasTree, toxic (hazardous waste), diaper, hedgeTreeTrimming (garden waste), collectionStation (a mobile collection point) or fleaMarket (reusable items); in the middle of a list.
notice.bins.fraction.en: {fraction, select, paper {Paper} bio {Food waste} residualWaste {Residual waste} residualWasteLessFrequent {Residual waste} residualWasteContainer {Residual waste} residualWasteContainerLessFrequent {Residual waste} reusableMaterials {Plastic} glassContainer {Glass and metal} christmasTree {Christmas trees} toxic {Hazardous waste} diaper {Nappies} hedgeTreeTrimming {Garden waste} collectionStation {Collection point} fleaMarket {Reuse} other {Other waste}}
notice.bins.fraction.nb: {fraction, select, paper {Papir} bio {Matavfall} residualWaste {Restavfall} residualWasteLessFrequent {Restavfall} residualWasteContainer {Restavfall} residualWasteContainerLessFrequent {Restavfall} reusableMaterials {Plast} glassContainer {Glass og metall} christmasTree {Juletrær} toxic {Farlig avfall} diaper {Bleier} hedgeTreeTrimming {Hageavfall} collectionStation {Miljøstasjon} fleaMarket {Ombruk} other {Annet avfall}}
